# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/update-config-docs.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Every flag `one` accepts and every environment variable one-cli reads. The [manual](manual.md) and [permissions](permissions.md) pages explain how they fit together.

## Flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-h`, `--help` | show this help message and exit |
| `-p`, `--print` | Non-interactive mode: print prompt answer and exit. |
| `--feedback-fd` | Inherited private feedback socket for headless turns. |
| `--mask` | Named task mask; use --masks to list, off to disable. |
| `--masks` | List task masks without contacting a provider. |
| `-m`, `--model` | Backend name or model id (see --list). |
| `--ui`, `--theme` | Terminal animation: braid-stream, patternflow-port, orb-pulse, scan-line, equalizer; also accepts legacy banner themes. |
| `--orchestrator` | Run the top-level agent on NAME and send every unpinned subagent to --model instead. 'none' (the default) runs everything on --model. |
| `--orc` | An orchestration config: which backend drives and which backend each subagent preset runs on. A name is looked for in ./.orc.json and ~/.one-cli/orc.json; a path is read directly. Explicit flags still win. |
| `--orc-list` | Print every orchestration config this run could resolve - name, orchestrator, worker pins and the file it came from - then exit. |
| `--orc-show` | Print one orchestration config in full, resolved against the presets this run would load, then exit. A `workers` entry naming a preset that does not exist is flagged rather than silently ignored. |
| `--orc-report` | Summarise every run record in ~/.one-cli/runs and exit - median wall time, steps and tokens grouped by backend and task class, with the failure-mode counters beside them. Runs no model. |
| `--effort` | Reasoning effort via backend-declared profiles; auto uses task policy. |
| `--task-class` | What KIND of work this run is, recorded on the run record so runs can be grouped later. Free-form; research, build, review, refactor and debug are suggestions, not a list. Beats a `task_class` in the orc config. |
| `--phases` | Drive this run off a fixed checklist instead of one prompt: a JSON list of phases, as a path or inline. One implementer is re-steered phase by phase and each phase lands on the run record with its own start, end, verdict and cost. |
| `--phase-mode` | How the checklist is worked: 'loop' re-steers ONE long-lived implementer with its history carried forward, 'fanout' spawns a fresh one-shot child per phase. The two modes are measured as a paired comparison. |
| `--phase-wording` | Which sentence each phase is asked with. Recorded on every phase, because a claim about prompt wording that cannot be told apart afterwards is untested. |
| `--phase-agent` | The preset the implementer runs as. Its pin decides the backend, exactly as a task tool call would. |
| `--orc-explain` | Print the resolved orchestration config in full - every preset, the backend it landed on, which rung decided it, and the file it came from. |
| `--model-id` | Override the model id on the resolved backend, so one endpoint can serve several models (a provider's tiers). |
| `--base-url` | Explicit endpoint, bypassing discovery. |
| `--wire` | Which protocol the endpoint speaks. Default openai. |
| `-w`, `--workspace` | Directory the agent works in. Default cwd. |
| `-s`, `--max-steps` | Tool-loop budget. Default: no limit. |
| `--response-gate` | First-response policy; default enforce for one CLI. |
| `--meditate` | Review the draft once using read-only evidence within the existing step budget. |
| `--progress-seconds` |  |
| `--progress-tool-calls` |  |
| `--no-progress` | Disable progress checkpoints. |
| `--max-tokens` | Output ceiling per model call. Default: none is sent, so the provider allows the model's own maximum. |
| `--temperature` | Sampling temperature. Default: none is sent, so the provider's own default for the model applies. |
| `--timeout` | Per-request timeout in seconds. |
| `--read-only` | Withhold write, edit and bash from the model, and refuse them at call time if it names one anyway. |
| `--guard` | Program consulted before every tool call. Reads the call as JSON on stdin; exit 2 blocks it and stderr is the reason. Uses Claude Code PreToolUse payloads; only exit zero allows execution. Repeatable; the first block wins. |
| `--guard-timeout` | Per-guard time limit. Default 10.0. A guard that overruns fails closed and is reported. |
| `--ask`, `--no-ask` | Let the model ask you a question when it hits a fork it cannot resolve. Default on in interactive mode, off otherwise - a one-shot run has nobody to ask. |
| `--ask-timeout` | How long a question waits for you. Default 300. On a timeout the model is told to decide alone and say what it assumed. |
| `--repeat-limit` | Identical tool calls before the model is told it is repeating itself. Default 3; 0 turns the reminder off. Advisory - it never blocks. |
| `--discovery-limit` | Consecutive tool rounds with no write, edit, question or spawned work before the model must commit to a target or ask one clarifying question. Default 6; 0 turns the checkpoint off. |
| `--tool-deadline` | Per-call ceiling. Lowered into any tool that declares a timeout, and reported as an advisory for one that sets its own clock. Default 120s; 0 disables. |
| `--image` | Attach an image to the turn. Repeatable. |
| `--audio` | Attach an audio file (a voice note) to the turn. |
| `--video` | Attach a video to the turn. No wire we speak carries video, so the Senses Eye perceives it as text. |
| `--media-route` | How attachments reach the model: auto (inline when the backend has the sense, else perceive it as text), inline, describe, transcribe, off. Default auto. |
| `--no-media-fallback` | Take the first rung of a media ladder or fail. Without it a route climbs down to the next rung. |
| `--inline-audio` | Send raw audio to a backend that declares it, instead of the transcript. The transcript is the default because it is the path proven on every backend. |
| `--speak` | Synthesize the final answer through pocket-tts and print the file path. Default voice alba. |
| `--autocompact`, `--no-autocompact` | Summarize the oldest messages away when the history nears the model's context window. On by default. |
| `--compact-at` | Fraction of the context window that triggers a compaction. Default 1.0: only when the next request would not fit the model's window. |
| `--context-window` | Override the model's context window. Default is the measured value for known models, else 131072. |
| `--compact-keep` | Messages kept verbatim after a compaction. The real cut is walked back from here so no tool result loses the assistant turn that called it. Default 6. |
| `--max-budget-usd` | Stop the loop once the run has cost this much. Only meaningful for a model with a known price. |
| `--max-input-tokens` | Maximum cumulative metered input across the run (cache reads at their price ratio, default 0.1). Default: no cumulative input ceiling; 0 disables. |
| `--require-priced-budget` | Reject missing/invalid prices or budgets before model execution. Requires --no-fallback. This validates the existing post-response budget, not a hard spending ceiling. |
| `--request-budget-policy` | Operator-audited text request tariff/bounds. Requires a durable ledger. |
| `--request-budget-ledger` | Shared durable request reservations; reopening never resets budget. |
| `--request-budget-isolated` | Tool-free one-shot request-budget profile; disables hooks, MCP and children. |
| `--request-budget-sandbox-grant` | Host-owned CodingGrant JSON for bounded offline tools; requires isolated budget mode. |
| `--create-request-budget-ledger` | Explicitly initialize request budget storage for a new work item. |
| `--fallback-model` | The chain a turn walks down when a backend is overloaded, rate-limited or unreachable. Comma separated and repeatable; `auto` (the default) ranks what discovery already found, `off` pins the run to one backend. A model declining the task is not a failure and never spends a rung. |
| `--on-unavailable-model` | When the model named with -m is offline or fails: `ask` (default; a terminal offers online alternatives, otherwise as `error`), `error` (exit 2 with the alternatives), or `fallback` (switch to the first online alternative and say so). Host default: ONE_CLI_ON_UNAVAILABLE_MODEL. |
| `--fallback-allow-paid` | Let `--on-unavailable-model fallback` switch to a paid lane. Host default: ONE_CLI_FALLBACK_ALLOW_PAID=1. |
| `--no-fallback` | Stay on one backend. What a benchmark wants: a cell that answers on a spare is measuring the wrong model. |
| `--permission-mode` | How careful this run is. `default` runs every tool; `acceptEdits` is the same surface (one-cli never stops to ask); `plan` withholds every mutating tool and asks for a plan instead of edits; `bypassPermissions` skips the allow/deny lists but still runs --guard; `readOnly` is --read-only. |
| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Skip permission prompts; alias for --permission-mode bypassPermissions. |
| `--allowed-tools`, `--allowedTools` | Tool patterns the model may call, Claude Code syntax: Read, 'Bash(git *)', 'Write(src/**)'. Repeatable and comma-separated. A non-empty list is a whitelist. |
| `--disallowed-tools`, `--disallowedTools` | Tool patterns that are refused. Beats --allowed-tools on a call that matches both. |
| `--add-dir` | An extra directory the file tools may reach. Repeatable. Passing any of these turns the workspace plus these directories into the only readable roots. |
| `--no-project-context` | Do not discover and append CLAUDE.md files. |
| `--done-check` | Shell command, run in the workspace, that must exit 0 before a final reply counts as done. A failure is fed back to the model (3 times, reset by a tool call); after that the run ends as unverified, exit 1. |
| `--hooks` | Extra Claude Code shaped settings.json to read hooks from. User settings are also read. Named files are trusted executable configuration. Repeatable. |
| `--trust-project-config` | Allow this workspace's .claude/settings*.json hooks and .mcp.json servers to execute on the host for this run. Only use after inspecting and trusting the project. |
| `--mcp-config` | MCP servers to connect, as a Claude Code shaped settings file or an inline JSON object. Repeatable. Named configs may execute commands. Project .mcp.json requires --trust-project-config; --strict-mcp-config still excludes it. |
| `--strict-mcp-config` | Use only the servers named by --mcp-config, ignoring the project's .mcp.json. |
| `--agents` | A JSON file of named subagent presets, each with a description, an optional system prompt, an optional tool list and an optional max_steps. Repeatable. The built-in 'general' and 'explorer' are always present. |
| `--agent` | Run this session AS a named preset: its system prompt and its tool surface. The preset can only narrow what the run already had. |
| `--list-agents` | Print the subagents this run would offer (built-ins plus every --agents file) and the vendor CLIs a preset can name as its `driver`, then exit. |
| `--max-depth` | How deep subagents may nest. Default 2; 0 withholds the task tool entirely. |
| `--no-hooks` | Run no hooks at all, whatever the settings files say. --guard is unaffected. |
| `--system` | Replace the system prompt. |
| `--system-file` | Replace the system prompt with the contents of a file. For a parent process with a large prompt to inject: an argv string is capped at 128KB by the kernel, a file is not. Refused alongside --system. |
| `-r`, `--resume` | Continue a session. Bare -r resumes the newest. |
| `--json` | Emit one JSON object on stdout instead of prose. |
| `--stream` | Print the answer as it arrives. Default on when stdout is a terminal and neither --json nor --quiet is set. With --json, stream transport progress on stderr while keeping one final JSON object on stdout. |
| `--no-stream` | Wait for the whole turn before printing anything. |
| `--text-events` | With --json --stream, include public answer text deltas on stderr for a streaming UI. Never includes reasoning. |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Suppress the step trace; print only the answer. |
| `--plain` | No colour, no box-drawing. Same as NO_COLOR=1. Already the default when stdout is not a terminal. |
| `-c`, `--chat` | Chat instead of work: a question and an answer, with a tool loop underneath it rather than a run around it. Read tools run freely; bash asks before running. `one-chat` is the same session with a tenth of the startup, and takes --tools. |
| `--list` | List reachable backends. |
| `--session-search` | Filter saved sessions by name or opening prompt. |
| `--sessions-here` | List sessions in the selected workspace. |
| `--sessions` | List saved sessions. |
| `--version` | show program's version number and exit |

## Environment variables

### Backends

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HF_TOKEN` | Hugging Face token sent when the serving catalog reads model metadata. |
| `ONE_CLI_API_KEY` | API key for a backend given with `--base-url` on the command line. |
| `ONE_CLI_LANE_HEALTH` | Lane health state file shared across processes (default `~/.config/one-cli/lane_health.json`). |
| `ONE_DEFAULT_BACKEND` | Backend name to use when none is chosen with `-m`. |
| `ONE_DEFAULT_MODEL` | Fallback for `ONE_DEFAULT_BACKEND` when that is unset. |
| `ONE_MODELS_DIR` | Directory for GGUF model weights used by local serving; created if missing, and used instead of the default search locations. |

### Terminal

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `EDITOR` | Editor for `/edit` in the chat; `VISUAL`, then `vi`, when unset. |
| `ONE_CLI_CALLER` | Names the program that launched `one`, for session records; otherwise read from the parent process on Linux. |
| `ONE_NO_MOUSE` | `1` turns off mouse support inside tmux. |
| `ONE_PLAIN` | `1` turns off the full-screen terminal UI and prints plain lines. |
| `TMUX` | Set by tmux; read to route clipboard copies and mouse handling through it. |
| `VISUAL` | Editor for `/edit` when `EDITOR` is unset. |

### Media

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` | Enables Deepgram as a hosted transcription fallback. |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | Enables Groq as a hosted transcription fallback. |
| `GROQ_STT_MODEL` | Groq transcription model (default `whisper-large-v3`). |
| `ONE_CLI_VISION_BACKENDS` | Comma-separated backend names to use for describing images, in order. |
| `ONE_PARAKEET_REMOTE_URL` | Speech-to-text server with the same API, probed only when `ONE_PARAKEET_URL` is unset (a set `ONE_PARAKEET_URL` is used as given); no default. |
| `ONE_PARAKEET_TIMEOUT` | Seconds to wait for a transcription (default 120). |
| `ONE_PARAKEET_URL` | Base URL of a speech-to-text server: any server that answers `GET /health` and takes a multipart `file` upload at `POST /transcribe`, returning JSON `{"text": ...}`. No default. |
| `ONE_SENSES_DESCRIBE_BUDGET` | Total seconds for describing one attachment (default 30). |
| `ONE_SENSES_DESCRIBE_MAX_TOKENS` | Token cap for an image description (default 1200). |
| `ONE_SENSES_DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT` | Seconds per image description request (default 15). |
| `ONE_SENSES_FRAME_BUDGET` | Most frames described per video (default 6). |
| `ONE_SENSES_LOG` | Media routing log file (default `~/.one-cli/senses_log.jsonl`). |
| `ONE_SENSES_MAX_VIDEO_BYTES` | Largest video file accepted (default 256 MiB). |
| `ONE_SENSES_MAX_VIDEO_SECONDS` | Longest video accepted as an attachment (default 600). |
| `ONE_SENSES_OLLAMA_ENDPOINTS` | Comma-separated Ollama URLs probed for vision models (default loopback only). |
| `ONE_SENSES_SECONDS_PER_FRAME` | Video seconds per described frame, below the frame budget (default 10). |
| `ONE_TTS_ENDPOINTS` | Text-to-speech ladder as a comma-separated list of `name=url=shape`. |
| `ONE_TTS_REMOTE_URL` | Text-to-speech endpoint used when no other is configured; no default. |
| `ONE_TTS_SHAPE` | API shape of `ONE_TTS_URL` (default `elevenlabs`). |
| `ONE_TTS_TIMEOUT` | Seconds to wait for speech synthesis (default 30). |
| `ONE_TTS_URL` | Pins one text-to-speech endpoint and disables the ladder; `ONE_TTS_SHAPE` names its API. |
| `ONE_TTS_VOICE` | Default voice for `--speak` (default `alba`). |

### Integrations

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ONECLI_NO_PRESENCE` | Set to 1 to disable endpoint presence probes and refusal checks; lanes remain unchecked. |
| `ONE_DETACHED_OWNER` | Set to `caller` when a parent process owns background jobs and route selection: one-cli then builds no fallback chain and starts no local detached workers. See [progress policy](progress-policy.md#parent-processes). |
| `ONE_INFER_BUDGET_DIR` | Where the scoped inference engine keeps its durable budget ledgers (default `~/.local/state/one-cli/infer-budget`). |
| `ONE_INFER_CONFIG` | Scoped inference engine config (default `~/.config/one-cli/infer.json`); without it every inference call is refused. |
| `ONE_INFER_LEDGER` | Scoped inference call ledger, one row per attempt (default `~/.local/state/one-cli/infer_calls.jsonl`). |

### Evaluation

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `KILO_BIN` | Path to the Kilo CLI, overriding the one found on PATH. |
| `MIMOCODE_BIN` | Path to the MiMo Code CLI, overriding the `mimo` found on PATH. |
| `ONE_CLI_ANALYSIS_DIR` | Where run analysis records go (default `~/.one-cli/analysis`). |
| `ONE_CLI_CORPUS` | Task corpus directory for the benchmark tools. |
| `ONE_STRESS_DIR` | Scratch directory for `one-stress` (default `.scratch/stress`). |
| `ONE_STRESS_LOG` | File the `one-stress` stub writes every request body to. |
| `ONE_STRESS_PORT` | Port of the `one-stress` stub provider (default 18642). |

### Advanced

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ONE_BINDING_FD` | Set by one-cli for a code-mode program: the socket its tool binding talks over. Not for users. |
